candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest predicts MALWARE with probability 1.0000, and all 20 top n-grams push toward cryptojacking, with no counter-evidence among them. The strongest cluster is SSE2 vector XOR and move activity: PXOR MOVUPS (+0.012850, the top feature and the most frequent at 0.001161), PXOR PXOR (+0.008983), LEA PXOR (+0.007472), MOVUPS PXOR (+0.006805) and MOVQ PUNPCKLQDQ (+0.007831). Together these suggest repeated 128-bit state mixing, as in hashing or cipher-style inner loops. A second cluster of integer bit-manipulation and carry patterns also points to hash-like arithmetic: XOR ADC (+0.009333), ADD ROR (+0.007020), ROL MOVZX (+0.006800), SHL NEG (+0.009044), SAR JNZ (+0.006744), SUB CMOVG (+0.010713) and MOVSXD BSR (+0.006819). A third cluster is floating-point activity, both x87 (FSTP MOV +0.012617, MOV FLD +0.010084, FSTP FSTP +0.006581, ADD FLD +0.006537) and SSE scalar (CVTSI2SD PXOR +0.006623, MOVAPD DIVSD +0.006164). Mixed integer, vector and floating-point compute of this kind is consistent with a compute-heavy mining kernel. Caveats: the evidence contains no function names or API context, and most n-grams have very low frequencies (many below 0.00005). Individually these mnemonics also appear in ordinary compiler output, so the tier rests on the model's output and the combined pattern rather than on any single decisive indicator.
